title: SCSS Investment Rules: Avoid These 5 Mistakes Before Investing ₹30 Lakh
description: The Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) currently offers an attractive interest rate of 8.2% for the October-December 2026 quarter. Retirees can now invest.

faq.q: What is the current SCSS interest rate?
faq.a: For the October-December 2026 quarter, the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) offers an annual interest rate of 8.2%. This rate is fixed at the time of investment for the entire 5-year tenure.

faq.q: Who is eligible to invest in SCSS?
faq.a: Generally, individuals aged 60 years or above are eligible. Those aged 55-60 years who have retired under VRS or superannuation can also invest within one month of receiving retirement benefits. Retired defence personnel aged 50 and above are also eligible.

faq.q: What is the maximum investment limit for SCSS?
faq.a: An individual can invest a maximum of ₹30 lakh in the SCSS scheme across all their accounts. For joint accounts, the entire investment is attributed to the first account holder for the purpose of this limit.

Yes, the interest earned from SCSS is fully taxable as per your applicable income tax slab. Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) may apply if the interest income exceeds ₹50,000 (for senior citizens) or ₹40,000 (for others) in a financial year.

faq.q: Can I withdraw money from SCSS prematurely?
faq.a: Yes, premature withdrawals are allowed, but they come with penalties. The penalty varies depending on when you withdraw: 1.5% of the deposit if withdrawn after 1 year but before 2 years, and 1% if withdrawn after 2 years but before 5 years. No interest is paid if withdrawn within 1 year.

faq.q: How do I avoid TDS on SCSS interest?
faq.a: If your total income is below the taxable limit, you can submit Form 15H (for senior citizens) or Form 15G (for non-senior citizens) to your bank or post office at the beginning of each financial year to prevent TDS deduction on your SCSS interest.

faq.q: Can I open multiple SCSS accounts?
faq.a: Yes, you can open multiple SCSS accounts, but the total investment across all your accounts (including joint accounts where you are the first holder) cannot exceed the maximum limit of ₹30 lakh per individual.
